resources.string:
Runs commands with the same rights as "adb shell", through Shizuku. It is not root. Shell commands can read system information, list and manage apps, change Android settings, and also clear app data or uninstall apps. Able cannot undo what a command does.

Commands run only when you tap Run. A command stops when you tap Stop, when you leave this screen, or after 10 minutes. Commands cannot read from the keyboard (no interactive input).

The output keeps the last 5,000 lines. Your last 100 commands and your snippets are stored only on this device and are excluded from backups. Able's action history records each command and its exit status, never its output.
Start Shizuku (with Wireless debugging or a computer) and come back. The shell runs commands with ADB shell rights through Shizuku; Able cannot run them on its own.
Allow Able in Shizuku so it can run the shell commands you type. Nothing runs until you tap Run.
Shizuku is not installed or could not be opened.
Shizuku is no longer connected. The command was not run.

Shizuku is a separate app that lets other apps use Android\'s ADB shell rights after you start it with Wireless debugging or a computer. With it, shell commands can read system properties and diagnostics (getprop, dumpsys), list packages, change settings, grant or revoke permissions, clear app data and uninstall apps for the current user. It cannot change system partitions or do what needs root. You can revoke Able\'s access in Shizuku at any time.

Shell commands run with ADB shell rights. They can change system settings, revoke permissions, clear app data or remove apps, and Able cannot undo them.\n\nCommands run only when you send them. Able asks again before commands that look destructive, but this check cannot catch everything.
This command may make changes that Able cannot undo:

Able looks for commands that delete files, uninstall apps, clear app data, change settings or the display, write raw data, format storage or restart the device. Running the command is still your choice. The check is based on the command text only: it can ask about harmless commands and can miss risky ones.
Uninstalls an app or its updates
Restarts or shuts down the device
Changes display size, density or window settings
Copied the newest output only (older lines were too long to copy)
Type a command or pick a snippet. Nothing runs until you tap Run.
%1$d older lines removed (the last %2$d are kept)
No snippets. Add commands you use often.
\"%1$s\" will be removed from your snippets.
Puts the command in the input field without running it
